baseline_models.focus_anchor: The temporal construction links seeing `بأسنا` to the spoken pair `آمنا ... وكفرنا`, while `وحده` and `مشركين` define the two opposed allegiances.
baseline_models.mechanism: Direct perception of overpowering force precipitates a public declaration whose first half assigns exclusive trust to God and whose second half repudiates the former partner-making arrangement.

activation_trace.role: Eye or perceptive seeing supplies the initiating encounter rather than a merely reported warning.
Overpowering severity supplies the coercive object that precipitates the declaration.
Produced speech makes the response an overt and socially audible avowal.
Heart-resting assent supplies the inward content claimed by the spoken avowal.
Divine oneness without partner turns assent into an exclusive allegiance.
Disavowal and disengagement make the second clause a renunciation rather than generic unbelief.
Partner-making identifies the former theological allegiance being renounced.

changed_reading.before: They see punishment, believe in God alone, and reject their idols.
changed_reading.after: The sight of overpowering force triggers an emergency transfer of allegiance: exclusive trust is publicly claimed and the former partner-making relation is expressly disowned.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The verse moves from sensory `رأوا` through outward `قالوا` to the inward-state verb `آمنا`.
baseline_models.mechanism: The sequence distinguishes the event that compels speech, the speech act itself, and the settled trust that speech claims. Because force is already visible, the focus alone leaves correspondence between utterance and inward security unresolved.

activation_trace.role: Perceptual seeing supplies the external event that immediately precedes the claim.
Overpowering severity supplies the pressure under which the speech is produced.
Audible utterance marks what is externally established by the verse.
Security and heart-settling name the inward condition asserted but not independently demonstrated.

changed_reading.before: Their belief is simply announced after they see the punishment.
changed_reading.after: Their utterance claims that the heart has settled into security, but the coercive sight-to-speech sequence does not by itself prove that inward settlement.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: `كفرنا بما كنا به مشركين` takes the former associated objects or practice as the object of repudiation, opposite `بالله وحده`.
baseline_models.mechanism: A prior state of distributed participation is terminated: the speakers withdraw from what they had made co-participant and replace that arrangement with a sole allegiance.

activation_trace.role: Separation and singleness supply the replacement state of undivided allegiance.
Disengagement and disavowal supply the act that terminates the former relation.
Occurrence in past time locates partner-making as an acknowledged former state.
Participation shared among multiple parties supplies the relational structure being dissolved.

changed_reading.before: They now disbelieve in the beings they once worshipped.
changed_reading.after: They explicitly withdraw from a former shared-allegiance structure and assert a newly undivided relation to God.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus confession reverses the exact allegiance pattern stated earlier: in 40:12 God alone was met with rejection and association with assent, while 40:84 joins assent to God alone and rejection to what had been associated. The same lexical poles have exchanged objects only after punishment becomes visible.

activation_trace.role: Assent now attaches to the exclusive divine object.
Oneness without partner defines the newly professed allegiance.
Disavowal now targets the former associated objects or practice.
The old partner-making allegiance is named as the object renounced.
The same exclusive oneness supplies the condition that had previously elicited rejection.
Rejection of the truth supplies the earlier response to invocation of God alone.
Partner-making supplies the earlier condition under which assent was offered.
Assent attached to association supplies the opposite pole of the earlier pattern.

structural_cues: 40:12 and 40:84 share the four allegiance roots but reverse which object receives faith and rejection.
The reversal in 40:84 is temporally subordinated to seeing `بأسنا`.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the exact lexical inversion and the sight-triggered timing; I infer that the later formula exposes a crisis-conditioned reversal of their established polarity. A live alternative is genuine repentance whose lateness, rather than sincerity, is the defect.

changed_reading.before: The speakers formulate a new monotheistic confession under threat.
changed_reading.after: They utter a word-for-word polarity reversal of their prior allegiance pattern, but only when the force they had resisted is directly visible.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah stages escalating modes of disclosure: signs are made visible and denied, historical outcomes are available to reflective looking, possessed knowledge becomes an object of boast, and the mocked consequence encloses its mockers. In the focus, seeing finally produces avowal only because disclosure has become bodily inescapable severity.

activation_trace.role: Direct perception supplies the final, coercive mode of disclosure.
Overpowering severity turns disclosure from inspectable evidence into experienced consequence.
Assent is the response that appears only at the terminal evidential stage.
Making visible supplies an earlier divine disclosure that did not require punitive contact.
The opposite of recognition names the refusal applied to already shown signs.
Directed sight or reflection supplies the unused route of learning from prior outcomes.
Claimed disclosure to the knower supplies the self-sufficient epistemic possession displaced by punitive sight.
Descending evil that surrounds its target converts the mocked warning into an enclosing reality.
Mockery supplies the prior stance toward the very consequence that later becomes visible.

structural_cues: 40:81 asks which displayed signs are denied; 40:82 calls for looking at earlier outcomes.
40:83-84 moves without a subject reset from rejoicing in possessed knowledge and mockery to encirclement, sight of severity, and confession.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated disclosure verbs and the immediate 40:83-84 sequence; I infer an escalating evidential threshold in which only experienced consequence defeats denial. The live alternative is that direct sight confirms rather than replaces an earlier intellectual recognition.

changed_reading.before: Seeing punishment supplies convincing evidence and produces belief.
changed_reading.after: Belief appears at the end of a failed disclosure sequence: shown signs, reflective evidence, and warning were resisted until knowledge was displaced by inescapable punitive sight.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier context locates arrogant resistance in the heart or breast and figures it as stamped. That interior obstruction sharpens the focus distinction between what the speakers audibly say and the heart-security denoted by faith: force can reverse speech without demonstrating that the prior interior formation has been undone.

activation_trace.role: Produced utterance marks the externally observable level of the response.
Heart-settling security marks the interior state the utterance claims.
Sealing by a stamp supplies a durable interior obstruction rather than a momentary verbal posture.
The heart supplies the interior site whose state must be distinguished from spoken wording.
Pride and self-magnification supply the resistant disposition associated with the sealed heart.
The breast as the source from which acts issue locates pride beneath outward disputation.

structural_cues: 40:35 places sealing on every heart characterized by arrogance and domination.
40:56 says the disputants carry only pride in their breasts and will not attain its object.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an interior pride-and-seal mechanism and the focus supplies only its speakers' outward claim; I infer that coercion may alter the latter without evidencing removal of the former. The materially live alternative is sincere inward faith that is real but temporally ineffective.

changed_reading.before: The declaration transparently reports a newly believing interior.
changed_reading.after: The declaration is certain as speech but uncertain as evidence of an unsealed, settled heart; the context makes outward reversal and inward transformation separable.

context_deltas.mechanism: Effective response is presented earlier as a turn that continues by following a traversable way, whereas the focus compresses response into an utterance after severity is seen. The next ayah repeats faith, seeing, and severity, negates benefit, and places that negation on a recurring course; correct content has arrived after the interval for enacted following has closed.

activation_trace.role: Assent supplies the correct content whose timing and enactment are being tested.
Following behind supplies duration and enacted continuation beyond an initial turn.
A path extended for travel supplies the practical course on which response must continue.
Benefit as the opposite of harm supplies the expressly negated efficacy of the late response.
The repeated assent root identifies the very faith professed in the focus as ineffective at this point.
Repeated direct seeing pins the loss of efficacy to the same perceptual trigger as the focus.
Repeated overpowering severity fixes the boundary at experienced punishment.
A running, followed course generalizes the closed response window beyond a single episode.

structural_cues: 40:7 coordinates repentance with following God's path before protection from punishment.
40:85 repeats the focus sequence `faith + when they saw + Our severity` and explicitly negates its benefit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an enacted path model and an explicit terminal non-benefit rule; I infer that the missing element is not correct wording but time for response to become followed practice. An alternative is that lateness alone is decisive regardless of any implied path.

changed_reading.before: The speakers make the right confession, but inexplicably too late.
changed_reading.after: Their formula has correct content but occurs after response can unfold as turning and path-following; experienced severity marks a recurrent closure point at which assent no longer averts harm.

context_deltas.mechanism: An earlier judgment-scene answer first locates the associated objects, then erases the past claim with `we were not calling anything`. The focus instead uses the same past-state construction to acknowledge `what we had been associating` before disavowing it. Read thematically, crisis speech moves from disappearance and denial of the objects to ownership and repudiation of the former act.

activation_trace.role: Overt speech supplies the later crisis answer being compared with the earlier answer.
Disavowal supplies an active repudiation that differs from simply denying a past relation.
Past occurrence supplies explicit ownership of a former state.
Shared participation names the former practice that is finally acknowledged.
The interrogation explicitly raises the missing partner-making objects and practice.
Produced speech supplies the earlier defensive answer in the judgment scene.
The same past-state construction is used there to negate rather than acknowledge former conduct.
Calling by speech names the former practice that the earlier answer claims never occurred.

structural_cues: 40:73-74 asks where the associated objects are and answers that they vanished, then says `we were not calling anything before`.
40:84 instead says `what we were associating`, retaining rather than deleting the past-state predicate.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two plural crisis speeches with opposed uses of a past-state construction; I infer a thematic movement from erasure to admission and renunciation. The major live alternative is that the scenes involve different groups, so this is a surah-level speech pattern rather than one group's chronological confession.

changed_reading.before: The final clause merely rejects former objects of worship.
changed_reading.after: The final clause can also mark a late shift from evasively erasing the past to owning the former association precisely in order to repudiate it.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads repeated sight language as a political-epistemic mechanism. It remains anchored because 40:29 couples a ruler's `showing/seeing` claim to claimed guidance, while 40:84 uses collective direct sight of God's severity; downstream prose should present this as a possible collapse of mediated vision, not assert that the same speaker or group persists.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The plural `رأوا بأسنا` can contrast unmediated collective sight with the earlier ruler's claim to show others only what he himself sees.

activation_trace.role: Direct collective perception supplies a sight no longer filtered through another speaker's opinion.
Overpowering severity supplies the reality that defeats control over what may be seen.
Showing and making visible supply the ruler's paired claim to control both presentation and perception.
Direction toward a path ties the ruler's curated sight to his asserted monopoly on guidance.

changed_reading.before: A condemned group finally sees divine punishment.
changed_reading.after: Their collective direct sight may also stage the collapse of an earlier regime in which authority claimed to determine what others could see and treat as guidance.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because it activates the hunter's snare image within `شرك`. It remains anchored to `مشركين`, the disavowal branch of `كفرنا`, and exclusive `وحده`; downstream prose should render it only as a material analogy for desperate extrication, not as the lexical sense of the verse.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: `وكفرنا بما كنا به مشركين` can carry an exploratory image of trying to disengage from an entangling partnership only after overpowering danger is seen.

activation_trace.role: A hunter's entangling snare supplies the exploratory material image of the former association.
Disengagement and renunciation supply the attempted motion out of that entanglement.
Separation and singleness supply the claimed state after extrication.
Overpowering severity supplies the moment when the entanglement is recognized as fatal.

changed_reading.before: The speakers renounce their former partners.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the speech resembles a last attempt to cut free from an entangling partnership at the instant its fatal capture becomes visible.

strongest_changes: The exact inversion of 40:12 turns the focus confession into a delayed reversal of an established allegiance polarity.
The 40:81-84 disclosure sequence distinguishes signs and reflective evidence from the coercive sight that finally defeats denial.
The path model of 40:7 and the explicit ruling of 40:85 show why correct confessional content can arrive after its effective response window.
Heart-and-seal cues preserve a live distinction between an outwardly certain declaration and an inward transformation that the declaration alone cannot verify.
summary.what_was_special: The focus reuses the surah's own faith, rejection, oneness, association, sight, and severity roots in a tightly reversed formula, and the following ayah repeats the sight-triggered faith event while directly denying its benefit.
remaining_uncertainties: The packet does not decide whether the declaration lacks inward sincerity or is sincere but temporally ineffective.
The 40:73-74 denial-to-admission pattern may connect distinct condemned groups only thematically.
The curated-vision and snare models are useful cross-domain activations but should remain explicitly exploratory.
